summary.text: Jessie Weatherley is the One Nation candidate for Eltham at the 2026 Victorian election. She runs her own marketing consultancy, where she is creative director, after earlier senior corporate roles, and has served as president of a local school council. Her party page lists crime, parents' say in schooling, aged care and state spending as her focus.

lives.note: The ABC says she has lived in Eltham for 12 years; her party page says 20 years in the local area.

occupation.text: Owner and creative director, marketing consultancy

priorities.text: Reducing crime so people feel safe at home and in public
A greater say for parents in what schools teach, with a focus on literacy and numeracy
Aged care that treats older people with dignity
Accountable, transparent state spending and lower debt
Being part of the solution to local problems rather than only complaining about them

sources.title: Eltham: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

priorities.text: Tougher animal protection laws, covering wildlife and farmed animals, and accountability for cruelty
Banning duck shooting and greyhound racing
Protecting the environment for future generations
A more sustainable and affordable society
Equality and inclusion, so that everyone is treated with dignity

summary.text: Louise Brooksby is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Eltham at the 2026 Victorian state election. Her party page says she was born and raised in Eltham, runs a small business and has four children. Tougher animal cruelty laws are her main cause, alongside the environment and equal treatment for all people.

sources.title: Louise Brooksby for Eltham, Animal Justice Party Victoria
Eltham, 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Maeve Riches is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Eltham at the 2026 Victorian election. She describes herself as a renter, a student and a hospitality worker who belongs to the United Workers Union. She says she became active through the climate movement and has since campaigned on LGBTQIA+ rights, refugees, Palestine and opposition to the far right.

priorities.text: a society that puts people before profit
Properly funded public services and affordable, adequate housing
Redirecting money from fossil fuel subsidies and AUKUS
Easing cost-of-living pressure on working people

sources.title: Eltham: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Paul Byrnes is the Liberal candidate for Eltham at the 2026 Victorian election. He works as a lawyer for the Commonwealth on national security and emergency management, and was earlier an adviser to former Liberal MPs Matthew Bach and Mary Wooldridge. He grew up in Eltham North and has a long involvement with Scouts Victoria.

sources.title: Eltham: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Paul Byrnes, Liberal for Eltham, Liberal Party of Australia (Victorian Division)

summary.text: Rachel Busbridge is the Greens candidate for Eltham at the 2026 Victorian election. She lectures in sociology at a university, is an environmental advocate and says she has been a union advocate for staff and students. She moved to Eltham in 2019.

prior_roles.role: Union advocate for university staff and students

priorities.text: Climate action, including protecting Eltham's tree canopy and wildlife
Getting the community ready for higher bushfire risk
More investment in public and active transport
Better-funded schools and health care as the area grows
Representation built on integrity, evidence and listening to residents

sources.title: Eltham: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Rachel Busbridge, Candidate for Eltham, Australian Greens

summary.text: Steven Marasea is the Libertarian candidate for Eltham at the 2026 Victorian election. He is a registered builder in a family business and says he has lived in Eltham with his family for a decade, having grown up in nearby Templestowe. His party profile centres on less bureaucracy, lower taxes and smaller government.

priorities.text: Cutting red tape that holds up builders and small businesses
Lower taxes and smaller government
Parents' freedom to raise their children as they choose

sources.title: Eltham: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Our 2026 state election candidates, Libertarians Victoria

summary.text: Vicki Ward has held Eltham for Labor since 2014, after many years on the staff of federal Labor MP Jenny Macklin. She entered the ministry in 2023; her current portfolios are creative industries, which she took on in April 2026, and public transport, added in August 2026. She is recontesting Eltham in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Minister for Emergency Services; Natural Disaster Recovery; Equality
Minister for Prevention of Family Violence; Employment

prior_roles.note: Parliament dates this from 2020; Wikipedia's infobox starts it in 2022.

prior_roles.role: Parliamentary Secretary for Public Transport Infrastructure
Parliamentary Secretary for Industry and Employment
Adviser and electorate officer to Jenny Macklin MP

priorities.text: Good services, facilities and infrastructure across the Eltham electorate
Government helping people create opportunities and supporting those doing it tough
Strong, connected local communities and volunteering
